source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Explore barriers, provide collaborative education, and discuss long-acting injectable options when suitable","B":"Increase the antipsychotic dose automatically whenever the client reports feeling better on treatment","C":"Avoid discussing adverse effects because attention to side effects generally reduces medication adherence","D":"Defer adherence planning until another relapse occurs because current symptom control is sufficient"}}
source_row.rationale: Schizophrenia treatment guidance supports collaborative attention to adherence, patient preferences, treatment barriers, and use of long-acting injectable antipsychotics in appropriate patients, especially when adherence is a concern.
source_row.source_detail: APA schizophrenia guideline: treatment planning, adherence, shared decision-making, and long-acting injectable antipsychotic considerations; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: American Psychiatric Association — Practice Guideline for Treatment of Patients With Schizophrenia
source_row.stem: A client with schizophrenia repeatedly stops medication after symptoms improve. Which strategy best supports long-term adherence?
